sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and the State.

2. By means of this application, the Petitioner seeks grant of anticipatory bail Under Section. 438 of Cr.P.C. in apprehension of arrest for his alleged involvement in the offences U/s. 498- A/323/294/506/420/509/34 of IPC and Section-4 of D.P. Act corresponding to C.T. Case No. 532 of 2023 arising out of Mahila P.S Case No. 50 of 2023 pending in the file of learned S.D.J.M.,
Bhubaneswar.
3. Perusal of the FIR reveals that the Informant married to the present Petitioner on dated 11.02.2020, after marriage, she lived happily with their in-laws.
But, after 05 months they demanded more money from her parental house and also demanded an Audi Car but, her parents were unable to fulfill their demand.
On 02.07.2020, the Informant left her in laws house and stayed at her parental house, after that her husband tried to compromise the // 2 // matter and bring her back to his house.
Then her husband took her nude photograph and black mailed her to viral the same in social media and forged her signature and filed a mutual divorce case against her wishes.

4. Keeping in view the submission of the parties, the nature of allegations as emerged from the materials on record, the circumstances appearing, the seriousness and gravity of the offences, this court is not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the Petitioner.
Accordingly the prayer for bail stands rejected and the ABLAPL is dismissed.
(Chittaranjan Dash) Judge B.K Sahoo Location: High Court of Orissa Jitendra Rout vs State Of Odisha
